title: Stakeholder-mapped SLO rollout playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This playbook codifies a stakeholder-mapped approach to rolling out SLOs across product teams, platform, customer success, and infra. Goal: reduce ambiguity during rollout, align expectations with product owners and GTM, and create reproducible rollout lanes (pilot -> cohort -> org-wide). This doc is intentionally pragmatic: it lists roles, a light-weight timeline, checklists for each lane, gating criteria, communications templates, and key runbooks to attach to each service.

Context and problem statement:
- Multiple teams serving inference endpoints have different expectations about latency, availability, and cost tradeoffs.
- Past SLO rollouts stalled because of unclear stakeholders, missing observability coverage, and no agreed escalation path to SRE.
- We need a repeatable pattern for services of different criticality (Tier A/B/C) so we can scale SLO adoption without heavy bespoke coordination.

Principles:
- Stakeholder first: every service rollout must have an identified product owner, platform owner, and SRE liaison.
- Minimum viable SLO: start with one latency and one error budget SLO for a pilot.
- Observability as code: instrument dashboards and alerts as part of the PR that creates/changes SLOs.
- Fast feedback loops: include customer-success and solutions engineering in pilot retros to capture external impacts.

Stakeholder mapping (roles and responsibilities):
- Product owner: defines user-facing significance, approves SLO targets, coordinates customer communications.
- Service owner (engineering): implements telemetry, traces, and config changes; responsible for on-call playbook updates.
- SRE liaison: validates alerts, constructs runbook, ownership transfer checklist, and signs off on gating criteria.
- Platform/infra: ensures quotas, autoscaling and routing policies aligned with SLOs (batching/quantization knobs if applicable).
- Customer Success/Support: prepares customer-facing notes and triage escalation paths for pilot customers.
- Product Security/Compliance (as needed): reviews changes that affect data residency or logging.

Rollout lanes and gating criteria:
1) Pilot lane (4 weeks): 1-2 services; 1 high-touch customer or internal team.
   - Preconditions: telemetry coverage >= 95% of requests, latency histograms present, error classification tags.
   - Gating: 2-week stability window with error budget consumption < 20% week-over-week and no P0 triggered by instrumentation changes.
   - Artifacts: SLO PR, dashboard link, runbook, customer-facing note.

2) Cohort lane (6-8 weeks): 4-6 services of similar criticality.
   - Preconditions: pilot retro completed, platform playbooks refined, automated SLO creation scripts validated.
   - Gating: cohort run shows < 40% error budget consumption across services and latency p95 within target for 2 consecutive weeks.

3) Org-wide lane (6-12 weeks per org wave): scoped by business unit.
   - Preconditions: cohort sign-off, rollout template baked into CI (observable-as-code), training for on-call rotations.
   - Gating: executive sign-off on aggregated risk, runbook catalog published, automated alerts propagated to PagerDuty / Opsgenie with documented escalation.

Sprint-style timeline (example pilot for inference-routing service):
- Week 0: Kickoff workshop (stakeholder mapping, target SLOs, risk log) — Product + SRE + Platform + CS.
- Week 1: Telemetry sprint — add latency buckets, error codes, and trace sampling; publish dashboard draft.
- Week 2: Alert tuning and runbook drafting; create SLO PR and peer review.
- Week 3: Canary enforcement with traffic split (10% -> 30%); observe error budget burn.
- Week 4: Pilot retro, customer impact check, decision: promote to cohort or rollback.

Checklists (copyable) — Pilot readiness checklist:
- [ ] SLO definition documented (objective, SLI, window, target, stakeholder)
- [ ] Telemetry coverage >= 95% (logs, traces, histograms)
- [ ] Dashboards created (latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate, burn-rate)
- [ ] Alerts with initial thresholds created and routed to SRE queue
- [ ] Runbook drafted with steps for triage, rollback, and communication
- [ ] Customer-facing note template prepared
- [ ] Capacity/infra constraints documented (quotas, burst capacity)

On-call and escalation playbook (summary):
- Primary triage: SRE on-call for 30 minutes to classify impact.
- If customer-visible degradation (product owner confirms impact): escalate to product owner and CS lead within 15 minutes.
- For automated rollback: include a single-command traffic-shift runbook with ownership and permission list.

Communications templates (short examples):
- Pilot announcement to stakeholders:
  "We're starting a 4-week pilot for SLOs on <service>. PO: <name>. Key targets: p95 latency < X ms, availability > Y%. Weekly checkpoints Fridays 11:00. Escalation: SRE PagerDuty."
- Customer-facing incident stub:
  "We are investigating increased latency impacting inference calls to <service>. We have mitigations in place and will provide updates every 30 minutes. If you are a pilot customer, contact <CS lead> for workspace-specific guidance."

Training and enablement:
- SLO office hours: weekly 1-hour drop-in for teams doing pilot work (SRE facilitators).
- Playbook lab session: 2-hour hands-on where teams implement an SLO from instrument to alert to runbook in a test env.
- SLO authoring checklist and example repo (link in linked_artifacts).

Quality gates and observability acceptance tests:
- Each SLO PR must include an automated smoke test that validates metric emission under synthetic load.
- CI job: run lightweight replay of typical request distribution and assert latency histogram buckets exist.

Risk register (top items):
- Incomplete telemetry: delays launch; mitigation: telemetry sprint and monitoring QA sign-off.
- Alert fatigue: too many noisy alerts during rollout; mitigation: SRE-led tuning window and rate-limited notifications.
- Capacity surprises: SLOs cause throttling/backs-off that impact downstream; mitigation: platform capacity guardrails and canary traffic splits.

Decision and escalation matrix:
- Project-level decisions (threshold changes, rollback) made by Product + SRE + Service owner.
- Escalation to Eng Director if aggregated error budget burn > 50% across pilot services for > 48 hours.

Success metrics (how we measure adoption):
- % of Tier A services with at least 1 SLO and runbook in the catalog within 6 months.
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for SLO breaches improves by 30% in pilot cohort.
- Number of customer-impact incidents related to telemetry gaps reduced by 80% for piloted services.

Attachments and next steps:
- Attach SLO template PR, dashboard templates, runbook template, communications templates to the Confluence playbook (linked_artifacts).
- Next steps: schedule kickoff with candidate pilot teams (suggested: inference-router, embeddings-ingest) and book first SLO lab.

Notes to reviewers (open questions):
- Do we require a mandatory security review for any telemetry that includes identifiers? (Proposed: yes for Tier A).
- Should the platform team create default SLO configs for standardized infra-backed services? (Proposed: create opt-in defaults for 80% of cases).

Sign-off: 
- Proposed sign-off workflow: SRE liaison completes checklist -> Product owner acknowledges user impact -> Platform confirms infra readiness -> Eng director final sign-off for cohort promotion.
